outputs.L2: An isolated DC–DC converter comprises a substrate and a transformer having primary and secondary windings. A primary-side circuit is formed by the primary winding, a primary-side electronic component, and primary-side wiring. A secondary-side circuit, which is electrically insulated from the primary-side circuit, is formed by the secondary winding, a secondary-side electronic component, and secondary-side wiring, with the secondary-side electronic component including a choke coil. The converter further includes an inter-circuit electronic component and inter-primary-side-circuit wiring that extend between and connect the primary-side and secondary-side circuits while maintaining DC isolation between them. The choke coil is positioned at a distance from one principal surface of the substrate. Located in the space between the choke coil and that principal surface are: (i) at least one of the primary-side electronic component and the inter-circuit electronic component, and (ii) at least part of either the primary-side wiring or the inter-primary-side-circuit wiring.
outputs.L3:
The insulated DC-DC converter includes a substrate on which a transformer having primary and secondary windings is provided. A primary-side electronic component and associated wiring are electrically connected to the primary winding to form a primary-side circuit. Similarly, a secondary-side electronic component and associated wiring are electrically connected to the secondary winding to form a secondary-side circuit that is electrically insulated from the primary-side circuit.

The secondary-side electronic component includes a choke coil arranged at a distance from one principal surface of the substrate. At least one electronic component belonging to the primary-side circuit or disposed between the primary-side and secondary-side circuits, together with at least part of its associated wiring, is positioned in the space between the choke coil and the principal surface of the substrate. This arrangement allows the available space beneath the choke coil to be used efficiently, thereby supporting a more compact converter configuration.
outputs.L4:
An insulated DC-DC converter includes a substrate on which a primary-side circuit and a secondary-side circuit are formed. The primary-side circuit receives a DC input and drives a transformer, while the secondary-side circuit rectifies and smooths the transformer output to produce an electrically isolated DC output. A choke coil is connected to one of the circuits to suppress current ripple or noise. The converter also includes at least one inter-circuit component, such as an isolation transformer, an isolating signal coupler, or a safety-rated capacitor, that transfers energy or signals between the primary and secondary circuits while preventing a direct DC connection.

The choke coil is mounted above the substrate so that a usable space is created between the lower surface of the coil and the substrate. One or more selected components associated with the primary-side circuit, or with the insulated interface between the primary and secondary circuits, are positioned within this space. Conductive wiring belonging to the primary-side circuit or the isolated interface may likewise extend beneath the choke coil. Thus, when viewed perpendicular to the substrate, the choke coil overlaps at least part of the selected components or wiring.

This vertically overlapping arrangement uses space that would otherwise remain unoccupied beneath the elevated choke coil. It therefore reduces the mounting area required by the converter and permits a smaller, more densely integrated power-supply module. At the same time, the primary-side components and conductors remain separated from the secondary-side circuit by appropriate insulation distances, insulating materials, and component placement. The resulting structure achieves compact packaging without compromising the DC insulation required between the input and output sides of the converter.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest yet most frequently used words in the English language. It is known as the definite article because it points to a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “a book” may refer to any book, while “the book” identifies a particular one.

Although “the” often goes unnoticed, it gives language clarity and precision. It helps speakers distinguish between something general and something already known. This simple word demonstrates how even the smallest elements of language can play an essential role in communication.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing the component layout and electrical isolation structure of an insulated DC-DC converter with a transformer and choke coil.
counterfactuals.output: An insulated DC-DC converter includes a circuit substrate, a transformer, a choke coil, and a plurality of switching and rectifying components mounted on the circuit substrate. The transformer includes a primary winding electrically coupled to an input-side circuit and a secondary winding electrically coupled to an output-side circuit, the primary and secondary windings being separated by an insulation barrier. The choke coil is disposed adjacent to the transformer and connected in series with an output-current path. The circuit substrate includes an input-side conductive region, an output-side conductive region, and an isolation region extending therebetween. Conductive patterns and component terminals associated with the primary side are spaced from conductive patterns and component terminals associated with the secondary side by predetermined creepage and clearance distances. An insulating member is interposed between at least portions of the transformer, the choke coil, and the circuit substrate to suppress electrical discharge and magnetic or capacitive coupling. The arrangement provides a compact component layout while maintaining galvanic isolation between the input and output terminals.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a single formal claim for an isolated DC-DC converter in which primary-side components or wiring are positioned between a raised secondary-side choke coil and the substrate.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention involving a substrate-mounted insulated power converter, including primary and secondary circuits, an inter-circuit component, and a choke coil spaced from the substrate.

It includes electrically isolated primary and secondary circuits, a component connecting or coupling the two circuits while maintaining insulation, and a choke coil positioned with a gap above the substrate. This spaced arrangement improves electrical insulation, heat dissipation, and component layout while enabling compact power conversion.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, using precise patent terminology, the architecture of a compact isolated DC-DC converter that uses the space beneath a choke coil to accommodate primary-side or isolation-related components and wires.
counterfactuals.output:
A compact isolated DC–DC converter may comprise:

- a printed wiring board having a primary-side circuit region and a secondary-side circuit region separated by an electrical-isolation boundary;
- an isolation transformer mounted on the printed wiring board and having a primary winding electrically coupled to the primary-side circuit region and a secondary winding electrically coupled to the secondary-side circuit region;
- a choke coil mounted above a first major surface of the printed wiring board, the choke coil including a magnetic core and a winding and being supported such that a clearance space is defined between a lower surface of the choke coil and the first major surface of the printed wiring board; and
- at least one primary-side circuit element, isolation-related circuit element, and/or insulated conductor disposed within the clearance space and within a plan-view projection, or mounting footprint, of the choke coil.

The primary-side circuit element may include a switching device, gate-drive component, snubber component, rectifying element, or input-side passive component. The isolation-related circuit element may include an isolation capacitor, optocoupler, digital isolator, transformer terminal, or component associated with feedback across the isolation boundary. The insulated conductor may comprise a jumper wire, winding lead, bus conductor, or interconnect routed beneath the choke coil.

The choke coil is preferably elevated by its terminals, a bobbin, a core holder, or an insulating support member. An electrically insulating sheet, coating, encapsulant, or molded barrier may be interposed between the choke coil and the underlying element or conductor so that prescribed clearance and creepage distances are maintained. By arranging such elements in the otherwise unused volume beneath the choke coil, the converter reduces its board-mounting area while preserving galvanic isolation between the primary-side and secondary-side circuits.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
